findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the OUTBOUND differ also skips any local comment carrying `jira_comment_id` (inbound-origin) — the outbound path MUST consult the inbound-origin field, so correct the §1b claim that 'the two never need to consult each other' and add its coverage to an AC.
evidence: Plan §1b: 'The two never need to consult each other' and the map is 'the map's ONLY consumer' for the outbound direction.

Plan Scope: 'comment differ keyed by the ID map (via the local comment key) instead of the normalized body key (:143)' and 'This replaces the fragile outbound body-equality membership test ... with ID identity while leaving BOTH the inbound differ and the inbound jira_comment_id field as-is.'

outbound_comments.py:371-406 — today an inbound-origin local comment is skipped ONLY because its normalized body is in `jira_bodies`; RECONCILER_MARKER is NOT on inbound-origin bodies (it decorates outbound echoes only, and inbound pull strips it via _normalize_comment_body, :174).
_processors.py:354-356 — inbound-origin local comments carry `jira_comment_id`, NOT an outbound-map entry, so the map cannot identify them.
findings.finding: The outbound differ loses its only loop-breaker for inbound-origin comments: removing the body-equality membership test and replacing it solely with the outbound map (which has no entry for inbound-origin comments) causes every inbound-mirrored comment to be re-pushed to Jira as a duplicate.
findings.location: Approach §1b / Scope: outbound_comments.py (_diff_comments :143 keyed by map instead of body)
scenarios: A Jira comment is mirrored inbound into rebar (gets jira_comment_id, no outbound-map entry); the next outbound pass finds no map entry for its HLC key and re-creates it in Jira — duplicating a comment that originated in Jira.
findings.suggested_fix: In the outbound differ, skip a local comment when EITHER (a) its local HLC key is already a key in the outbound map, OR (b) it carries a `jira_comment_id` field (inbound-origin). Add an AC asserting an inbound-origin comment (has `jira_comment_id`, no map entry) is not re-pushed outbound (extend test_comment_bidirectional_identity_no_double_sync to cover exactly this local-comment shape).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `outbound_differ.py` (`compute_outbound_mutations` → `_diff_comments` call at `:741`) to Scope as the site where the real `RichTextCodec` is threaded into the `codec=` argument, rather than flipping the `_resolve_codec` default in `outbound_comments.py` (which would regress a32a's no-codec baseline tests).
evidence: Plan Scope lists only `outbound_comments.py` for 'flip the `_diff_comments` a32a codec injection (`_resolve_codec`)' and does not list `outbound_differ.py`.

Code: `outbound_differ.py:741` — `comment_mutations = _diff_comments(ticket, jira_key, comment_snapshot, client=client, inbound_mapper=inbound_mapper)` passes NO `codec=`, so it resolves to `_IdentityCodec`.
a32a completion comment: 'nothing wires a real codec into `compute_outbound_mutations` — verified: `grep codec outbound_differ.py` returns nothing ... injecting the real codec is a one-line change.'
`_diff_comments` signature at outbound_comments.py:223-231 shows `codec: Any | None = None` with the default resolving to `_IdentityCodec`.
findings.finding: The codec-injection flip attributes the change solely to `outbound_comments.py` (`_diff_comments`'s `_resolve_codec` default), but the real production injection is made by the CALLER via the `codec=` argument. `_diff_comments`'s sole production call site — `compute_outbound_mutations` at `outbound_differ.py:741` — passes NO `codec=` today (so it defaults to `_IdentityCodec`). Flipping the injection to the real `RichTextCodec` requires editing `outbound_differ.py:741`, which is absent from the plan's Scope file list. This is confirmed by the a32a ticket's own completion note: 'nothing wires a real codec into compute_outbound_mutations ... injecting the real codec is a one-line change.' Flipping the default inside `outbound_comments._resolve_codec` instead would silently alter every other caller — including a32a's baseline test that pins identity behavior when no codec is injected.
findings.location: Scope: `outbound_comments.py` — 'flip the `_diff_comments` a32a codec injection (`_resolve_codec`) from `_IdentityCodec` to the real `RichTextCodec`'
scenarios: outbound_differ.py:741 (the sole production caller of _diff_comments) is left un-patched, so production comment-diff keeps using _IdentityCodec and the dedup-key migration AC (test_comment_dedup_key_uses_real_codec / test_dc_comment_diff_converges_after_migration) is never exercised on the production path.

If the flip is instead applied as a new default inside outbound_comments._resolve_codec, a32a's baseline test test_without_an_injected_codec_todays_baseline_behaviour_is_unchanged and test_diff_comments_codec_normalization.py's no-codec cell break, because they assert identity behavior when no codec is injected.
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope, add `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` — pass the real `RichTextCodec` into the `_diff_comments(...)` call at `:741` (inside `compute_outbound_mutations`) so the production comment-diff routes the local dedup key through `normalize_outbound`; leave `outbound_comments._resolve_codec`'s `_IdentityCodec` default intact so a32a's no-codec baseline tests stay green.

findings.finding: The Scope locates the codec-injection flip in outbound_comments.py (_resolve_codec), but the actual injection is made by the caller via the codec= argument. _diff_comments's sole production caller is _compute_outbound_update_mutation at outbound_differ.py:741 (passes no codec), and the create-path renderer _map_comments_for_create is called at outbound_differ.py:624 with only `ticket`. outbound_differ.py is absent from Scope/file_impact, so the real patch site for both 'flip to real RichTextCodec' and 'render create bodies via to_wire' is unenumerated.
findings.location: Scope — outbound_comments.py bullet: 'flip the `_diff_comments` a32a codec injection (`_resolve_codec`) from `_IdentityCodec` to the real `RichTextCodec`'; AC line 5
findings.suggested_fix: List src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py in Scope: pass the deployment's RichTextCodec as codec= at _diff_comments (:741) and thread it into _map_comments_for_create (:624) so both outbound comment call sites use the real rendering codec.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify where/when the newly-recorded comment id is durably persisted (e.g. save() after the create-path comment loop, or acknowledge/close the successful-create-then-crash re-post window) so the ID-map approach retains the body-key approach's crash idempotency.
evidence: dispatch_one.py:405-428 — the create-path comment loop runs AFTER the last in-function `binding_store.save()` (:295) and `bind_confirm` (:309); there is no save() after the comment loop.
reconcile.py:607 — the binding store is persisted only at end-of-pass; a crash between a successful add_comment and that save loses the in-memory map entry.

dispatch_one.py:414-417 comment: the current single-attempt design relies on 'a failed post falls to comment_errors and is re-emitted by the comment differ next pass' — self-healing that the body-key match made duplicate-free but the empty-map-on-restart does not.
Plan Scope for the create path says only 'call binding_store.record_comment_id(...)' and 'keep the non-fatal comment_errors behavior' — no persist point or crash-window discussion.
findings.finding: The ID-map identity abandons the body-key approach's self-healing crash idempotency without specifying when the returned id is durably persisted, opening a create-succeeded-then-crash window that re-posts the comment on the next pass.
scenarios: add_comment succeeds in Jira, the process is killed before the end-of-pass binding_store.save(); next pass the map has no entry for that HLC key, so the differ re-creates the comment in Jira — a duplicate.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist the map immediately after a successful add_comment records an id (or document that the end-of-pass save at reconcile.py:607 is the persist point and add an AC covering the create-succeeded-then-crash-before-save case: a restart must not re-post an already-created comment). Consider that idempotence AC test_comment_sync_idempotent only covers the clean re-pass, not the crash-mid-pass case.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the crash/retry semantics of the create-then-record path (durability ordering of record_comment_id vs. the Jira write, and behavior under at-least-once retry) and note whether reconciler passes are serialized so the check-then-record is race-free.

no statement about atomicity/ordering or crash-safety between the Jira create and the local record_comment_id write

findings.finding: The create-then-record sequence (Jira add_comment succeeds, then binding_store.record_comment_id writes the mapping) has an unaddressed crash/durability window: if the process fails between the successful Jira create and the durable map write, the next pass sees no map entry and re-creates the comment, breaking the append-only/idempotence guarantee.
scenarios: Reconciler crashes or is killed after Jira accepts the comment but before record_comment_id is flushed; the following pass re-posts the same comment.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that reconcile passes are serialized (no concurrent map mutation) and add a reconciliation fallback (e.g. detect an already-posted RECONCILER_MARKER comment for the local key before creating) so a lost record_comment_id write does not re-post.

scenarios: A binding that already mirrored comments before this change runs its next reconcile pass; existing rebar comments have no map entry and get posted to Jira a second time.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the encode/sanitize ordering on the Cloud comment path so `_sanitize_comment`'s 32767-char guard still bounds the landed payload (mirror acli.py:205's sanitize-plain-text-then-ADF composition rather than json.dumps'ing a post-truncation dict).
evidence: Plan: '--body json.dumps(to_wire(body)), mirroring acli.py:205'

acli_cli_ops.py:479 `body = _sanitize_comment(body)` runs before the send; docstring cites bug 6afc: 'ACLI exits 0 on an over-length rejection, so an unguarded body fails silently and re-emits every pass'
AdfCodec.to_wire returns an ADF dict (rich_text_codec.py:33-35); _sanitize_comment is typed str->str (jira_fields.py:56)

The mirrored description path (acli.py:205) sanitizes plain text INSIDE _text_to_adf(_sanitize_description(...)), i.e. it truncates plain text before ADF conversion — an ordering the comment path does not currently mirror
findings.finding: The plan's new Cloud comment ADF-encode step (`--body json.dumps(to_wire(body))`) does not specify how it composes with the existing `_sanitize_comment(body)` char-limit guard in acli add_comment, which is a str->str 32767-char truncation (acli_cli_ops.py:479, bug 6afc). to_wire returns an ADF dict for Cloud, so ordering matters: encoding first feeds a dict into a str-typed sanitizer, while sanitizing first then json.dumps means the char-limit is measured on plain text but the wire carries the larger serialized ADF, so the guard no longer bounds the landed payload.
scenarios: An over-length outbound comment body on Cloud after the encode step is added
A comment body near the 32767 limit whose ADF serialization inflates past the char guard
findings.suggested_fix: Truncate the plain comment text via _sanitize_comment BEFORE to_wire, then ADF-encode: `body = json.dumps(to_wire(_sanitize_comment(body)))` for Cloud — matching acli.py:205's `_text_to_adf(_sanitize_description(...))` composition — and keep DC on the str path unchanged.

jira_family/__init__.py:24-26: 'Dependency direction is one-way: this package imports NOTHING from adapters/jira/ … no adf'
findings.finding: The plan mislocates the Cloud codec: it states the render seam `AdfCodec.to_wire for Cloud` lives at `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py`, but `AdfCodec` (and its `to_wire`, which wraps `adf.text_to_adf`) actually lives in `adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py`. Only `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` (DC) is in `jira_family/rich_text.py`. The `jira_family` package documents (rich_text.py:23-27, __init__.py:24-27, ADR 0035) that it imports NOTHING from `adapters/jira/`, so `AdfCodec` cannot be co-located there and cannot be imported from the shared layer.
findings.location: Approach step 2 / Scope (outbound_comments.py rendering bullet): 'the SAME RichTextCodec.to_wire seam … (adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py — AdfCodec.to_wire for Cloud, the now-rendering WikiTextCodec.to_wire for DC after 3388)'
scenarios: Implementer follows the cited path to add the comment-render wiring inside jira_family/rich_text.py and either cannot import AdfCodec/adf there (ADR-0035 seam violation) or edits the wrong file for the Cloud codec.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to: 'rendered through the shared `RichTextCodec` contract (`adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py`) — `AdfCodec.to_wire` (Cloud, `adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py`) / the now-rendering `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` (DC, `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py`) — injected into the comment path via the existing `_resolve_codec` seam (never imported by jira_family, per ADR 0035).'
